name: General Python Placement Assessment
description: A 40-question multiple-choice placement test spanning the full Python Apprentice and Python Games concept range. Used to place a prospective student into the right course and starting lesson.

placement_rubric.explanation: Score each band as a percentage of its questions answered correctly. Walk the bands in order; the student is placed at the START of the first band scoring below the mastery threshold. If every band is mastered, use 'placed_beyond'.

placed_beyond.note: Mastered all assessed Python content — ready for Python Games projects or the next level (Java). Recommend instructor review.

questions.question: What does turtle programming let you do?
options: Give commands to a virtual turtle telling it where to move and draw
Connect to the internet to download images
Edit photos taken with a camera
questions.answer: Give commands to a virtual turtle telling it where to move and draw
questions.explanation: Turtle programming lets you control a virtual turtle that draws on the screen, like a small robot artist.

questions.question: Which line creates a turtle named tina?
questions.explanation: tina = turtle.Turtle() creates a new turtle object named tina.

questions.question: Which two commands does the triangle exercise ask you to use to draw the sides?
questions.explanation: The 10_Turtle_Tricks exercise says to use tina.forward() and tina.left() to draw the three sides.

questions.question: How many times does the body of this loop run?
questions.code:
for i in range(4):
    print('Loop Iteration', i)
questions.explanation: range(4) generates 0, 1, 2, 3, so the loop body runs four times.

questions.question: Which description best fits a variable?
options: A labeled box that stores information you can change
A command that turns the turtle
A note for humans that Python ignores
questions.answer: A labeled box that stores information you can change
questions.explanation: The lesson describes a variable as a labeled box that stores information you can change anytime.

questions.question: What image format must you use for a custom turtle shape?
questions.explanation: The lesson states the image used as a turtle shape must be a GIF.

questions.question: What is a list in Python?
options: A built-in data structure that stores an ordered collection of items
A way to draw shapes with the turtle
questions.answer: A built-in data structure that stores an ordered collection of items
questions.explanation: A list stores an ordered collection of items.

questions.question: Where does the turtle module come from?
options: It is a pre-installed Python tool
You must buy it from a store
You build it yourself before class
It only works on the League Code Server
questions.answer: It is a pre-installed Python tool
questions.explanation: The lesson explains the turtle module is a pre-installed Python tool you use to control the turtle.

questions.explanation: Both values are strings, so + concatenates them into "1020".

questions.question: What does print(text[0:6]) display?
questions.explanation: The slice [0:6] takes characters at indices 0 through 5, which spell "Python".

questions.question: What does this print?
options: a is 11\na is 10\na is less than 20
questions.explanation: a == 11 is False, but a == 10 and a < 20 are both True, so two lines print.

questions.question: Which prefix marks a hexadecimal number in Python?
questions.explanation: 0x is the prefix for hexadecimal; 0b is binary and 0o is octal.

questions.question: Which call asks the user for their age as a whole number?
questions.explanation: askinteger() returns the user's answer as an integer.

questions.question: What is the overall goal of this program?
options: Ask for one number and double it
Ask for two numbers and display their sum
questions.answer: Ask for two numbers and display their sum
questions.explanation: The opening docstring says to ask for two numbers and display the sum.

questions.question: How many things does the program ask the user for?
options: Two numbers and a math operation
questions.answer: Two numbers and a math operation
questions.explanation: The docstring lists a number, a second number, and a math operation.

questions.question: How is Code Wars described compared to HackerRank?
options: More competitive and gamified, like a game for coding
questions.answer: More competitive and gamified, like a game for coding
questions.explanation: The lesson describes Code Wars as more gamified, with ranks and badges.

questions.question: What is an iterable?
options: Anything that can produce its items one at a time until nothing is left
A number that can only be used inside a loop
A special kind of variable that counts upward
A function that always returns True
questions.answer: Anything that can produce its items one at a time until nothing is left
questions.explanation: An iterable lets you get the first item, then the next, until none remain.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: range() returns a range object, so its type is range.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Indexes start at 0, so backpack[0] is the first item, 'map'.

questions.question: According to the hint, what must be true about the forwards, lefts, and colors lists?
options: They should all have the same number of elements
They must each have exactly three elements
questions.answer: They should all have the same number of elements
questions.explanation: Parallel lists read by a shared index must line up, so they need matching lengths.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a tuple and a list?
options: A tuple cannot be changed after it is created; a list can
A tuple can only hold numbers
A list uses parentheses and a tuple uses brackets
A tuple is always longer than a list
questions.answer: A tuple cannot be changed after it is created; a list can
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable, while lists are mutable.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Index -1 counts from the end, so it is the last item, 'orange'.

questions.question: What is the value of words[0] in this exercise?
questions.explanation: Index 0 is the first item in the list, 'Once'.

questions.question: What are triple quotes (""") specifically used for?
questions.explanation: Triple quotes let a string run across several lines.

questions.question: In a function definition, where does the function's name appear?
questions.explanation: The name comes right after def, as in def add_ten(x).

questions.question: What exception does this line raise?
questions.explanation: The string is the right type but cannot be converted, so it raises a ValueError.

questions.question: What does this code print for the set?
options: A set with all six items
questions.explanation: A set removes duplicates, so only the unique values remain.

questions.question: What data structure does this program use to store words and their definitions?
questions.explanation: The definitions are stored in a global dictionary called db.

questions.question: Given the array below, what does two_dimensional_array[1][2] return?
questions.explanation: Index [1] is the second row [4,5,6], and [2] picks the third element, 6.

questions.question: How is the Tic Tac Toe board stored?
options: As a 3x3 2D array (a list of lists)
As a single flat list of 9 items
questions.answer: As a 3x3 2D array (a list of lists)
questions.explanation: The board is built as a 3x3 grid where each cell starts as None.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
def add_ten(x):
    return x + 10

result = add_ten(5)
print(result)
questions.explanation: add_ten(5) returns 5 + 10, which is 15.

questions.question: What happens when this loop reaches the value 'Bob'?
options: It crashes with a ValueError before finishing the loop
It prints Converting Bob to an integer: 0
questions.answer: It crashes with a ValueError before finishing the loop
questions.explanation: int('Bob') raises an uncaught ValueError, ending the program.

questions.question: In a Pygame physics program, what does acceleration directly change?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is added to velocity each frame, and velocity then changes position.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between a class and an object?
options: A class is a copy of an object
A class is a blueprint and an object is built from it
An object is a blueprint for a class
They are exactly the same thing
questions.answer: A class is a blueprint and an object is built from it
questions.explanation: A class defines the type; an object is one instance made from that blueprint.

questions.question: What does a 2D vector contain?
options: An x value and a y value
questions.answer: An x value and a y value
questions.explanation: A 2D vector groups an x and a y together into one object.

questions.question: What is a sprite in Pygame?
options: A 2D image that represents a game object
questions.answer: A 2D image that represents a game object
questions.explanation: Sprites are the images that move around the screen.

questions.question: What are the three types of collision detection described in the lesson?
options: Bounding box, circle, and pixel perfect
questions.answer: Bounding box, circle, and pixel perfect
questions.explanation: These are the three approaches the lesson lists.

questions.question: According to the lesson, a surface is best compared to what?
options: A blank piece of paper you can draw on
questions.answer: A blank piece of paper you can draw on
questions.explanation: A surface is anything you can draw on, including the screen and images.

questions.question: What kind of motion does this code produce for the red square?
questions.code:
a = (-K * (x_pos - center)) / mass
velocity += a * d_t
x_pos += velocity * d_t
options: It moves at a constant speed forever
It oscillates back and forth around the center like it is attached to a spring
questions.answer: It oscillates back and forth around the center like it is attached to a spring
questions.explanation: The acceleration always points back toward the center, producing spring-like oscillation.
